belongs_to: Example 1 (3/4 of the orange colour is red): 'Observe the following bar model diagram showing the equivalence between 3/4 and 75%'; followed by the question 'Can you tell what percentage of the colour was made using yellow?'

belongs_to: Example 2 (Surya saves 2/5 of the prize money): 'Try completing Method 3 by filling the boxes'

Horizontal band framed above and below by two long horizontal black lines, with six vertical black lines crossing it at equal spacing (left end, then 1/5, 2/5, 3/5, 4/5 and the right end = 5 equal parts). A thin RED outline rectangle runs along the whole band (0 to 5/5). belongs_to: Figure it Out Q4: 'A group of friends is participating in a long-distance run. The positions of each of them after 15 minutes are shown in the following picture. Match (among the given options) what percentage of the race each of them has approximately completed.'
description: Race track drawn as one horizontal black line with a short vertical end-tick at each end: left end labelled 'Start' (below the tick), right end labelled 'Finish' (below the tick). No other ticks or numbers on the line. Four blue filled circles (black outline) sit on the line, each with a letter ABOVE it, left to right: A, B, C, D. Measured from the picture as a fraction of the Start-to-Finish length: A about 0.32, B about 0.53, C about 0.75, D about 0.95 (D is very close to the Finish tick). Below the line a row of SIX equal square boxes, evenly spaced, each holding one percentage, left to right: 55% ; 20% ; 38% ; 72% ; 84% ; 93% (six options for four runners; the student matches runners to options).
unclear: Positions of A, B, C, D are measured by eye from the page picture, so the fractions are approximate; the book gives no exact values.

belongs_to: 'Percentages Around Us' card: 'The human body, on average, is about 60% water by weight.'
description: Card on a grey background with a simple cartoon figure of a boy standing, arms at the sides: brown hair, orange face and shoulders; from the chest down to the feet (body, both arms and both legs) the figure is filled with a blue water texture with a wavy water line across the chest; head and upper chest are not filled. Caption in a yellow box under the picture: 'The human body, on average, is about 60% water by weight.' No scale or numbers inside the picture.

belongs_to: Example 6 (Kishanlal's target is ₹5000 a day): 'The percentage target achieved is visualised below.' Day 1: 2000 (left of the two pictures)

belongs_to: Profit and Loss: 'The picture below shows the journey of a sweater from the manufacturer to the customer and what the cost price (CP), the marked price (MP), and the selling price (SP) mean in each step.'
description: Left-to-right chain of FOUR illustrated panels, each with a dark-navy heading box above it and a navy-framed picture: (1) 'Manufacturing Unit' (garment workers sewing at tables, a delivery van); (2) 'Wholesale Store' (two men handing over a carton, shelves of folded cloth); (3) 'Retail Store' (a woman in a clothes shop holding a sweater); (4) 'Customer' (a smiling woman in a kurta with two shopping bags). THREE black arrows point right, one between each pair of neighbouring panels (1 to 2, 2 to 3, 3 to 4). Under each arrow a dotted vertical line leads down to a yellow price tag: under arrow 1 (Manufacturing -> Wholesale): CP: ₹230 ; MP: ₹255 ; SP: ₹253. Under arrow 2 (Wholesale -> Retail): CP: ₹253 ; MP: ₹310 ; SP: ₹300. Under arrow 3 (Retail -> Customer): CP: ₹300 ; MP: ₹480 ; SP: ₹430. (The SP at each step equals the CP at the next step.)
